maria: spinning up a quick validation thread for the SEA-2 cluster PCIe fabric/host interconnect sweep. want to run a short latency/throughput pass and kernel/driver sanity before handing to SRE. plan below — pls ack and add gaps. :eyes:

maria: steps I'm proposing:
1) node-level checks: `lspci -vv | grep -i pcie`, `dmesg | grep -i pcie` for errors, `ethtool -k` for offloads
2) nvlink/topology: `nvidia-smi topo -m` + run `nvlink_test` (microbench)
3) p2p latency sweep: use `ib_send_bw`/`ib_read_lat` between GPU hosts across ToR/leaf, record p50/p95
4) kernel/driver verification: ensure driver >= 535.xx, `modinfo nvidia` and `cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version`
5) perf burn: 5m continuous inference-like workload with current runtime build, capture p95 tokens & tail latency
6) If any p95 > 220ms (for long seq) or PCIe errors, block handoff and escalate.

akshay: ack. couple of notes — for (3) use the new `p2p-sweep.py` script (repo: infra/tools/p2p-sweep) it toggles path through spine vs local ToR. it also emits a CSV we can drop into grafana.

lee: +1. add `lspci -vvv` for Fatal/Non-Fatal err counters. also check BIOS iommu/aspms settings, last time we saw ASPM causing noisy p95s.

maria: good call on ASPM, add `cat /sys/module/pcie_aspm/parameters/policy` to step1. I'll update the runbook.

infra-bot: job started: pcie-fabric-sweep-1963456789, nodes: sea2-edge-01..08, run_id=job-SEA2-042, kicked by maria, ETA ~18m

jordan: FYI on cost — don't run the 5m perf burn on all 8 nodes at once if cluster is near spot reclaim threshold. maybe stagger by 2 nodes.

maria: good call, we'll stagger 2-at-a-time with 2m offset. akshay can you schedule the p2p-sweep accordingly?

akshay: scheduling now. command I'm running in case you want to reproduce locally:
```
python infra/tools/p2p-sweep/run.py --hosts sea2-edge-{01..08} --mode latency --stagger 120 --out /tmp/sea2-p2p.csv
```
will push results to `grafana/infra/sea2/p2p-sweep` after each pair finishes.

infra-bot: sea2-edge-01/02: p2p sweep complete. p95 latency (host-GPU): 86us, 92us. pci_e_err counters: 0. nvlink links: full width. uploaded /tmp/sea2-p2p-01-02.csv

lee: nice. can we get `nvidia-smi topo -m` output in the thread for 01? small paste helps correlate.

maria: paste from sea2-edge-01:
```
G   N0  N1  N2  N3  PHB
GPU0  X   NV2 NV2 SYS SYS
GPU1 NV2  X   NV2 SYS SYS
```
no SYS chokepoints, matches expected cabling.

akshay: running kernel check now. saw one node with driver 532.11 earlier in staging. if we find <535 we will bail and schedule driver rolling update.

infra-bot: kernel/driver check summary: sea2-edge-01..08 drivers: [535.32, 535.32, 535.32, 535.32, 535.32, 534.87, 535.32, 535.32]. sea2-edge-06 flagged (534.87) — opening issue #infra-SEA2-DRV-6

maria: thanks infra-bot. akshay, please exclude -06 from perf burn and flag for driver upgrade.

akshay: excluded -06. perf burn running on pairs: (01,02) then (03,04) then (05,07) then (08) to avoid -06. collecting p95 tokens.

infra-bot: perf-burn results appended:
- 01,02 p95 tokens/sec tail-lat: 18ms
- 03,04 p95 tokens/sec tail-lat: 21ms
- 05,07 p95 tokens/sec tail-lat: 19ms
- 08 p95 tokens/sec tail-lat: 20ms
(no node exceeded 220ms threshold)

jordan: looks green from cost/perf. next steps for handoff: update cluster runbook with driver-exception for node-06, add a short note to the oncall rotation to watch sea2 for spot reclaim over next 24h.

maria: I'm going to update the runbook and file the post-check ticket. can someone please add the grafana dashboard link and mark this thread resolved after the driver patch is scheduled? :white_check_mark:

lee: adding grafana link: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/infra/sea2-p2p-sweep?orgId=1

akshay: scheduled driver upgrade for sea2-edge-06 next maintenance window (2026-04-12 03:00 UTC). will post update after patch.

maria: thanks all — handing to SRE oncall. closing thread in 30m unless anything pops up. :shipit:
